result.title: EVIDENT: Evaluating Evidence Grounding in GUI Agents
result.summary: GUI agents are increasingly evaluated by whether they complete web tasks, but surface success can hide a critical failure: the final answer may not be supported by evidence observed during navigation. We introduce EVIDENT, an evidence-driven benchmark for evaluating whether GUI agents ground their decisions in observable web evidence. EVIDENT contains 220 real-world English and Korean tasks spanning semantic grounding, contextual inference, and visual grounding, each paired with human-curated evidence metadata specifying what must be verified. We further separate surface task completion from evidence-grounded success using three metrics: TSR, ESR, and GSR, which respectively measure outcome success, required evidence observation, and claim-level evidence support. Experiments on commercial and open-source GUI agents reveal substantial gaps between surface success and evidence-grounded success, especially in contextual and visual tasks. These results show that current evaluations can overestimate agent reliability and highlight the need to assess not only whether agents answer, but whether they verify.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 EVIDENT，一个面向 GUI agent 的证据驱动基准，包含 220 个真实网页任务与人工标注的必要证据元数据，并用 TSR、ESR、GSR 三个指标区分「表层完成任务」与「答案确有观察证据支撑」。
AI.relevance_reason: 它把答案是否真正使用观察到的视觉证据单独度量，是可直接借鉴的失败诊断与评价框架，有助于核查 VLM 推理中视觉旁路与「答案不使用所获证据」问题；但任务为 GUI 导航，未涉及 latent 状态，需自行判断迁移程度。
